Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. I wanted to capture the follow-ups and a short checklist so we can converge on the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem). Key takeaways from today: FinOps has strict data residency and audit requirements for model inputs that push you toward a private deployment, but you still want to understand cost/throughput tradeoffs if Dedicated could work.

Quick asks to unblock qualification (can you reply inline?):
- Do you need inbound connectivity into your network (we call this peering/privatelink) or is outbound-only to Redwood sufficient (our PrivateLink/NAT egress pattern)?
- Expected steady-state throughput (reqs/sec) and peak concurrent connections for inference?
- Do you have an existing IP allowlist process and can you provide a CIDR or current egress IPs?
- Any constraints on TLS termination (do you require customer-managed certs / HSM)?

I'm attaching a short network-requirements template and our private-deploy checklist to help gather specifics. Once we have answers we can have Karthik do a quick 30-min technical qual to map the options and scope effort.

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the recap. Answers inline below. I also attached our internal network diagram and a short security note.

- Inbound vs outbound: We need strictly inbound-restricted access from a compliance standpoint. Anything that keeps customer data inside our VPC except egress-only telemetry is preferred. So PrivateLink (AWS) or VPC peering that allows us to control routing is required; outbound-only patterns are unlikely to pass our SOC/legal review.
- Throughput: Typical expected steady state is ~60 req/s (latency-insensitive calls), peak bursts up to ~250 req/s for short windows (~2–3 min). Average payload sizes ~1–2KB per request.
- IP allowlist: We currently maintain an allowlist process but we prefer AWS PrivateLink to avoid having to manage long lists of external IPs. If peering is required we can provide the list — will need time to compile.
- TLS/HSM: We require TLS with customer-managed certs for any inbound endpoints. HSM-managed keys preferred for signing.

Attached: FinOps_network_diagram_v3.pdf and FinOps_security_notes.docx.

We will try to fill the network template by Thu 6/30, and Ava will coordinate with our infra team for the session with Karthik.

Subject: Re: Infra deployment paths — hosted vs dedicated vs private (technical clarifications)

Thanks Miguel — helpful details. A few technical clarifications from our infra perspective before the qual call so we can prepare concrete architecture diagrams: 

1) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering:
   - PrivateLink (AWS) gives you an interface endpoint in your VPC and avoids managing external IP allowlists. It also keeps traffic on the AWS backbone which is preferable for compliance. However, PrivateLink is typically best for cases where Redwood hosts the service (we expose an endpoint) and you call out from your VPC. Peering is more flexible for bidirectional connectivity if you need Redwood-initiated connections to your hosts.

2) Inbound model access pattern:
   - You mentioned "inbound-restricted access" — to confirm: will FinOps expect to send requests to a Redwood-managed endpoint inside your VPC (i.e., our infra lives in your VPC via PrivateLink) or will you host the model weights in your environment and we run a connector that initiates outbound connections to Redwood-managed control plane? These two patterns have different network + HA implications.

3) Egress/NAT & IPs:
   - If PrivateLink is the preference we need to know whether you plan to use cross-account endpoint services or same-account. Also please confirm any proxy/NAT devices that could break TLS passthrough if we offer TLS termination on our side.

4) Certs and key management:
   - We support customer-managed certs and can integrate with common KMS/HSM providers. Please confirm the KMS provider and whether you need HSM-backed private key operations.

5) Throughput and pods sizing:
   - Peak 250 req/s with 1–2KB payloads is modest but we need to know concurrent connections and acceptable p99 latency targets to size Dedicated vs Private properly. If you can share a p99 target (e.g., <200ms) that helps.

If you can answer points 2 and 3 ahead of the call we will prepare two reference architectures (PrivateLink-hosted endpoint vs Peering + customer-hosted connector) and an estimated monthly cost delta.

Would Fri 7/1 10:00–10:30 PT work for a quick technical qual?

— Karthik
